slice: exploring: monarchs, eels and loggerheads, each going with its kind's artifact of prior living

items.section: 4.6 A reaching's competency constant, a gathering's climbing
items.text: A year's monarchs are an overwintering generation and three or four summer generations; monarchs coming out in late summer and early fall are biologically and behaviorally different, not mating or laying eggs until the next spring, living some eight or nine months against three to five weeks for a summer adult, going up to three thousand miles south, eastern monarchs to oyamel fir forests in central Mexico and western monarchs to California's coastal groves, often to the exact same trees, and each making the round trip once, the monarchs arriving at those trees being the great-great-grandchildren of the monarchs leaving them the spring before. No monarch going south has a prior of its own there: a monarch's going is its kind's artifact of prior living with milkweed and with a winter forest, its stable form aiming an autumn monarch into healthy living, and a year's generations one same-existing-society going round one year.

items.section: 4.6 A reaching's competency constant, a gathering's climbing
items.text: European eels live as adults in Europe's fresh waters and go 5,000 to 10,000 km across the Atlantic to the Sargasso Sea to spawn, eating nothing on the way, diving to about 1,500 m by day and rising to about 200 m by night, some 3 to 12 km a day, a going of perhaps 18 months; of 26 eels with satellite tags from the Azores, 23 tags giving data, six reach the Sargasso Sea, the first direct evidence of adults there, and the eels' larvae drift back to Europe on the North Atlantic Drift. An eel's going is its kind's artifact of prior living, its stable form aiming an eel to where its kind's living opens, a depth going with day and night and a larva's drift going with a current, each a co-sequencing.

items.section: 6.8 Eight legs, five dimensions in two directions
items.text: Loggerhead turtles nesting on beaches where an instrument reads a like magnetic field are genetically like each other, more than turtles on beaches near each other or of a like environment, turtles on Florida's two coasts where an instrument reads a like field being genetically like each other too; the study's authors ask whether a turtle learns its home or its genome gives it. A self observing reads a going-with: a turtle's coming home is its kind's artifact of prior living and its own prior same-existing now-existing in it, an instrument's reading at a beach going with that from outside a turtle's surface, and learning-or-genome a store question over one artifact of living.
